filename: Two for one_ Partitioning CO2 fluxes and understanding the relationship between solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence and gross primary productivity using machine learning.pdf
title: Two for one: Partitioning CO2 fluxes and understanding the relationship between solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence and gross primary productivity using machine learning
code_availability: The SCOPE simulations and the codes for NEE partitioning are available at GitHub (https://github.com/Weiwei047/SIF_partitioning) or at zenodo (https://zenodo.org/record/6450447#.YlTl9NPMLtN).
testbed_rationale: The synthetic SCOPE simulations and tower datasets along with public Python scripts on GitHub and Zenodo provide a well-documented benchmark testbed for unmixing/partitioning land-atmosphere carbon fluxes (GPP and ER) from net ecosystem exchange and solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence.
pain_points: Lack of direct daytime observations of ecosystem respiration and gross primary productivity at ecosystem scales
Model structural error in empirical daytime and nighttime flux partitioning methods during extreme events (drought) or rapid management changes (harvest)
Light inhibition of ecosystem respiration (Kok effect) is not explicitly captured because including radiation directly in respiration causes equifinality
Observation noise in eddy covariance and remote sensing/in situ SIF data
Possible mismatch between satellite-derived LAI (overstory) and understory vegetation phenology in heterogeneous canopies
extraction_notes: The primary ML task is unmixing/partitioning Net Ecosystem Exchange into its gross components (GPP and ER) while simultaneously discovering the empirical ecosystem-scale GPP-SIF relationship via multi-task learning. Deep ensembles (1000 retraining runs) were used for structural uncertainty quantification.
